synopsis: Dense deep reinforcement learning (D2RL), reported by Feng et al. in Nature on 22 March 2023, achieved unbiased automated-road-vehicle evaluation reported as 10^3–10^5 times faster on highway and urban test tracks using an augmented-reality environment [f6848, f14163]. The method trains background agents and is presented among statistical approaches to shortening validation, with academic open-source code identified as typical tooling [f633, f425, f7279]. Chapter 9 recommends D2RL and naturalistic-adversarial environments for accelerated unbiased evaluation in the collision-mitigation test program, but the demonstrated evidence is only on-road, not off-road [f7275, f7079]. Legitimate evaluation claims require a large naturalistic dataset and a learned naturalistic behaviour model; Chapter 1 additionally identifies a known exposure distribution as necessary and unavailable for the 100+ job-site types [f7277, f7278, f352]. A 2026 Nature Communications paper in the same research line applies dense learning to overcome safety-performance stagnation, but the supplied fact does not establish off-road validation [f6849].
